summary: Huachuca Mountains summit lookout, Cochise County AZ; FFLA lists a gone ground lookout, and a SummitPost overview describes rocks and light brush on the summit today.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it gone as a ground lookout; SummitPost says the summit once held a lookout tower and is now rocks and light brush

access.note: Summit reached on foot by the Crest Trail and a spur; SummitPost calls the hike short. No closure found in sources. Wikipedia says the Coronado National Forest manages the Miller Peak Wilderness, but the summit's position against the wilderness boundary was not checked.

visit.trail_note: Crest Trail along the range crest, then a steep spur to the summit; SummitPost calls the hike itself short

events.note: Tucson Daily Citizen item of May 2, 1962, reprinted by Forest Lookouts, says the lookout would be flown to the top by helicopter

evidence.supports: Miller Peak is the highest mountain in the Huachuca range, about 10 miles south of Sierra Vista
evidence.quote: it is the highest mountain in the Huachuca mountain range
The Miller Peak Wilderness encompasses 20,190 acres and is managed by the Coronado National Forest

evidence.supports: summit once housed a lookout tower; now rocks and light brush
evidence.quote: The summit used to house a lookout tower, but is now a jumble of rocks and light brush.

evidence.supports: summit accessible via the Crest Trail
evidence.quote: The summit is accessible via the Crest Trail

evidence.supports: short steep spur from the Crest Trail to the top
evidence.quote: A spur off the main trail leads steeply to the top

evidence.supports: 1962 item: lookout to be flown by helicopter to the top, under deep snow
evidence.quote: The Miller Peak Lookout in the Huachuca Mountains will be flown by helicopter to the top of the mountain whose upper elevations still are covered by deep snow.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Miller Peak, Cochise County, Ground, Gone

notes_for_editor: Conflict on structure: FFLA lists a ground lookout; SummitPost says the summit once held a lookout tower. The story reports both. Height conflict: Wikipedia 9,470 ft, SummitPost 9,466 ft; the story gives both. No build date, design or staffing record in readable sources. Peakbagging Table 1 row Miller Peak (LO site) carries status code C (badly damaged), which sits oddly with the LO site label (building removed); not used. The 2011 Monument Fire burned the mountain's pines (Wikipedia), but no source ties it to the lookout, so it is left out. No photos recorded. The SummitPost page is a hiker's overview rather than a dated trip report, and its 'short' remark describes the hike as a whole, not the spur.
